## Summary

Solved T2 (Pythia-1B structured head pruning, condition B) with a BrainSurgery YAML plan:

- **`out/T2/plan.yaml`**: for each of the 16 layers, concatenates the two surviving row-blocks of `query_key_value.weight`/`.bias` (rows `0:3840` + `4608:6144`) and the two surviving column-blocks of `dense.weight` (cols `0:1280` + `1536:2048`) into temporary `*_pruned` tensors, then deletes the originals and `move`s the pruned tensors onto the original names (regex + capture groups across all layers for delete/move). Preflight and post-condition `assert` blocks check the original 8-head shapes/244-tensor count up front and the required 7-head shapes (layer 0 explicitly, plus all 16 layers via regex) and final 244-tensor count before the plan can write output.
- **`out/T2/model.safetensors`**: single-file output (244 tensors, float16), verified against a hand-computed reference — every pruned tensor is bit-exact to `torch.cat` of the specified slices, every other tensor is byte-identical to the input, and no `_pruned` leftovers remain.
- **`out/T2/REPORT.md`**: participant self-report, including the two non-obvious wrinkles — `concat`/`split` don't support the regex fan-out that `copy`/`move`/`delete` do (so per-layer blocks had to be generated rather than expressed as one regex rule), and `output.path` needs a `.safetensors` filename (not a directory) to avoid sharded output.

The plan ran successfully on its first execution against the real 244-tensor Pythia-1B checkpoint.
